topics.label: Lecture Introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, contextualising the importance and complexity of complement within immunology.

topics.label: Foundations and Central Role of C3 in Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, terminology, and pivotal C3 activation hub of the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream recognition pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that converge to activate C3 on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement Effector Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the downstream effector mechanisms by which activated complement destroys pathogens and drives immune clearance.

topics.label: Regulation and Host Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that restrict complement activation and protect host cells from damage.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the clinical consequences and disease presentations resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the evolutionary adaptations and specific mechanisms used by pathogens to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, concluding the lecture on complement and previewing the upcoming lecture.
